cases.question: Which button swings the sword?
cases.answer: The A button swings the sword.

cases.question: How much does the Blue Candle cost?
cases.answer: The Blue Candle costs 60 rupees in the documents: it can be purchased for 60 Rupees through a door one screen west of the Fairy Fountain route, and a 2nd Quest shop in section E-4 also sells it for 60 rupees.

cases.question: How many Heart Containers do I need to get the White Sword?
cases.answer: You need five Heart Containers to receive the White Sword, according to the Items document. The Overworld Quest 1 walkthrough says six heart containers are needed for the cave in that quest, and the Hyrule 3 document also states at least 5 Heart Containers.

cases.question: Which item can I find in Level-3 of the first quest?
cases.answer: In Level-3 of the first quest, you can find the Raft (its dungeon walkthrough says that going down the stairwell in the room below the compass room leads to the Raft). The Objectives for that dungeon also list obtaining the Raft, a Heart Container, and the third Piece of Triforce.

cases.question: How powerful is the Magic Sword?
cases.answer: The Magic Sword has Damage 4, making it the most powerful sword in the game and four times as powerful as the wooden sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers to receive it.

cases.question: How can I sail across the sea?
cases.answer: The Raft allows Link to cross lakes and oceans, but it can only be used at a Dock; neither of the 'double docks' triggers raft use.

cases.question: Is there somewhere my hearts get refilled without paying?
cases.answer: Yes. A Fairy enemy drop fills 3 of Link's hearts, and in the fairy ponds the fairy fills all of your heart meters.

cases.question: How can I win cash by gambling?
cases.answer: Enter the Money Making Game, which is reached by walking inside the tree in Hyrule 1 section D-2 or by bombing the cliff wall just left of center in Hyrule 2 section A-5, or by bombing along the middle of the north wall in Hyrule 6 section C-5.

cases.question: What does the old man in Level-4 of the first quest say?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: What can I buy at D-4 in section 2 of the overworld?
cases.answer: In Section 2 of the overworld (Hyrule 2, 2nd Quest), D-4 is a shop where you can buy Arrows for 80 rupees, the Magical Shield for 130 rupees, and a set of 4 Bombs for 20 rupees.

cases.question: What happens if I register my name as ZELDA?
cases.answer: Entering your name as "Zelda" when you start the game immediately begins the Second Quest without playing the First Quest. The documents describe the name "Zelda"; they do not say whether the spelling "ZELDA" in capitals triggers the same effect.

cases.question: Where can I buy the Blue Candle, and what can it be used for?
subqueries: Where can you buy the Blue Candle in Castlevania NES
What can the Blue Candle be used for in Castlevania NES
cases.answer: You can buy the Blue Candle for 60 Rupees by going one screen west through the door from the spot reached via the Fairy Fountain route in the Quest 1 overworld walkthrough. It throws a flame a short distance, can be used once per screen, lights up dark dungeon rooms, burns bushes in the overworld, burns trees to reveal secrets, and damages enemies.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Level-1 in the first quest and how do I defeat him?
subqueries: Who is the boss of Level 1 in the first quest of The Legend of Zelda NES
How do you defeat the Level 1 boss in the first quest of The Legend of Zelda NES
cases.answer: The boss of Level 1 in the first quest is Aquamentus. Strike his head six times with the Wooden Sword or three times with the White Sword, timing strikes between the energy orbs he emits from his horn. Only the Magical Shield absorbs the orbs, while the regular shield lets damage through; sword beams can hit any part of his body.

cases.question: What do I need to enter Level-4 in the first quest, and which item is inside?
subqueries: What do I need to enter Level 4 in the first Legend of Zelda quest on the NES?
Which item is inside Level 4 in the first Legend of Zelda quest on the NES?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: How do I beat the dragon boss?
cases.answer: The question is ambiguous because two bosses are dragons. Aquamentus shoots fireballs and is vulnerable to the Sword and Arrows, and it can also be killed by two Bombs. Gleeok has two to four heads: stab each head until it flies free, then destroy every attached head, dodging the flying heads' projectiles. Tell me which dragon you mean for more detail.

cases.question: How do I defeat Gleeok?
cases.answer: To defeat Gleeok, you must stab each attached head until it flies freely around the room, then destroy every one of the attached heads; a freed head can still threaten you but cannot be defeated on its own. Defeating the boss earns a Heart Container. The documents describe this same strategy for the two-, three-, and four-headed Gleeok bosses, with the four-headed version in Dungeon 8 requiring you to keep stabbing until every head is disconnected.

cases.question: How do I use the Hookshot?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: Can I ride a horse in this game?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: In the first quest, which dungeon has the Ladder?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: In the second quest, which dungeon has the Ladder?
cases.answer: The documents do not state which dungeon in the second quest contains the Ladder. Dungeon 6's objectives list obtaining the Ladder, and Dungeon 7's walkthrough says to collect the Ladder before entering, but neither says the Ladder is located in that dungeon. Dungeon 6 is the one whose objectives include obtaining the Ladder.

cases.question: How can I attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. You can also press the B button to use your selected subweapon.

cases.question: Which button do i have to press to attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword, which is the attack. The B button uses your subweapon instead.

cases.question: How can I atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing your sword. You can also press the B button to use your selected subweapon, such as the Magical Wand.

cases.question: how do i open the menu
cases.answer: Press the Start button to bring up the sub-screen menu, where Link can look at the map and change subweapon, etc. Press Start again to return from the sub-screen to the normal view.

cases.question: can i blow up walls with bombz?
cases.answer: Yes. The bomb can be used to blast holes in weak walls, and the documents describe bombing cliff walls and room walls to reveal hidden passages.

cases.question: how do i use my secondary item
cases.answer: Press the B button to use your subweapon. Only the item in the blue box on the sub-screen can be assigned to B, and you change that assignment by switching to the sub-screen with Start.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing your sword. You can also press the B button to use your selected subweapon.

cases.question: how can i heal?
cases.answer: You can heal by drinking a Red Potion or Water of Life, which fully refill your life bar, or by visiting a Fairy Fountain, where the fairy fills all your heart meters. Enemy fairies restore only 3 hearts. A medicine woman sells Red Potions and Water of Life in a cave if you have shown her the Letter.

cases.question: where do i find money?
cases.answer: The documents mention several places to get rupees: the Money Making Game is in a cave behind a bombable rock face immediately left of the start screen (zelda1:cheats:004). In the 2nd Quest, the Money Making Game is in a tree at Hyrule 1 D-2 (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-1:003), and a Red Moblin cave on Hyrule 8 B-4 in the 1st Quest gives 30 Rupees (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-8:001). Other spots include a secret cave at Hyrule 1 B-3 giving 30 Rupees (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-1:003) and a stairwell at Hyrule 8 B-2 leading to 10 Rupees (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-8:002).

cases.question: what is the best weapon?
cases.answer: The most powerful sword in the game is the Magic Sword, which deals 4 damage and is four times as powerful as the Wooden Sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers before he can receive it.

cases.question: how do i open a locked door?
cases.answer: One cheat says that in the first dungeon, you can immediately leave and come back, and the locked door will open. Otherwise, keys open locked doors, with each key opening one door, and in Dungeon 8 you unlock a locked door on the left by defeating the Wall Masters and proceeding there.

cases.question: what do i do if ig im stuck
cases.answer: Per the General Tips, if you are unsure how to proceed through a dungeon, bomb every wall that does not contain a door, since you will typically find passageways leading further in. Also, passages can lead to rooms in the "eyes" or unmarked rooms on the dungeon map.

cases.question: how do i defeat the dragon?
cases.answer: The dragon is Gleeok, a multi-headed dragon: you must attack each head, and when a head takes enough damage it detaches and flies around the room. The flying heads cannot be hurt, so dodge their projectiles and focus on the heads still attached to the body. Keep stabbing the attached heads until every one is disconnected.

cases.question: where do i get bombs?
cases.answer: In Quest 1 you can get Bombs by defeating the Moblins in the area near the Fairy Fountain until they drop them. Quest 2 notes also list getting some Bombs as an early step, and you can get replacement Bombs from a man in the Quest 1 Dungeon 6 resupply area.

cases.question: how do i unlock the bow?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, Dungeon 1, the Bow is in room O-1, which has Traps in each corner and a central stairwell surrounded by blocks. Push the left-most block aside to enter the stairwell, where the Bow is found. You'll need to purchase Arrows to use it unless you already bought them before finding it.

cases.question: how do i save my game?
cases.answer: To save, choose "SAVE" with Select and press Start on the Game Over options screen, which stores your accomplishments until you next play. You can also press Up (D-pad) and A simultaneously on the second controller from the sub-screen menu to quickly access the Save Screen.

cases.question: how do i get more hearts?
cases.answer: Heart Containers give an extra permanent heart to Link's life meter. In Quest 1, you can get the fourth Heart Container by burning a specific tree on the Lake Hylia coast, and the sixth by setting a bomb on a huge rock at the foot of the eastern mountains. Fairies also fill 3 hearts, and in fairy ponds they fill all your heart meters.

cases.question: can i buy a better shield?
cases.answer: Yes. A Magical Shield is sold in several shops, and it reflects more attacks than the starting Small Shield. In Quest 1, a shop reached by burning a tree sells it for 90 Rupees, and in the 2nd Quest hidden shops sell it for 90, 130, or 160 Rupees depending on location.

cases.question: how do i see in dark rooms?
cases.answer: Light dark rooms with a candle: the Blue Candle can light them but can only be used once per screen, while the Red Candle has the same effect with no per-screen limit. Candles light up dark rooms in dungeons.

cases.question: Which button do I press to jump?
cases.answer: Press the A button to jump in the air.

cases.question: How many spirit points does the windmill star cost?
cases.answer: The windmill star costs 5 spirit points to throw.

cases.question: How many lives does Ryu start with?
cases.answer: Ryu starts the game with two lives in reserve.

cases.question: What happens if the clock runs out before I finish a stage?
cases.answer: You lose one life if the timer runs out before you complete a stage.

cases.question: How can I get higher using just one wall?
cases.answer: Use the wall hop technique: jump toward and cling to a wall, hold the jump button, push away from the wall, then immediately push back toward it as you let go. If done correctly, you rise and cling to the wall higher than where you started, and repeating this can take you to the top of the screen.

cases.question: Who attacks me in Stage 2-3?
cases.answer: In Stage 2-3, you are first attacked by the enemy known as Bomberhead as soon as you enter the hall.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Stage 3-3?
cases.answer: The boss of Stage 3-3 (Act III) is Basaquer, who leaps back and forth across the room and periodically shoots a trio of darts.

cases.question: What does the fire wheel do and does it use spirit points?
subqueries: What does the Fire Wheel spell do in the NES game?
Does the Fire Wheel spell use spirit points (SP) in the NES game?
cases.answer: The Fire Wheel surrounds Ryu with a circle of fire that eliminates any enemy that contacts him. It requires no spirit points to use, but it replaces any secondary weapon you hold and disappears after five seconds.

cases.question: What is Ninja Gaiden called in Europe?
cases.answer: In Europe, Ninja Gaiden is known as Shadow Warriors.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press B to attack by swinging your sword, and you can attack low by squatting when you attack. Hold Up on the D-pad while pressing B to use a secondary weapon, which requires enough spirit points.

cases.question: how do i get more ninpo?
cases.answer: The documents don't use the term "ninpo" directly. They say spirit points power secondary weapons and are gained from blue tiles (5 points) and red tiles (10 points), so collecting those tiles is the closest documented way to build your spirit points. Red Spirit Points tiles appear in Stage 2-1 and Stage 2-2.

cases.question: how do i heal?
cases.answer: The documents mention health-restoring potions that you can collect. In Stage 4-2, a lamp on the left gives a potion that restores some lost health, and in Stage 3-1 an item over a dock segment is a health-restoring potion. Stage 2-2 has an insect item holding a health restoring potion, and Stage 5-2 has a candle above the first potion that contains one.

cases.question: why did i get sent back to 6-1?
cases.answer: Losing to any of the final bosses sends you back to Stage 6-1, regardless of how many lives you have left. Defeated bosses stay dead, so you will not have to face them again once you return.
